newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.13 pct in seesaw trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.13 pct in seesaw trade.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.13 percent to close at 1.0875 per dollar in seesaw trade with players speculating over dollar outflows in the commercial foreign exchange market, dealers said.
Players speculated that banks would have problems with dollar outflows because they had been holding short positions.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts at 1640 local/1940 GMT showed a $25 million surplus, but dealers expected it would turn into a deficit at the end of the day.
Despite the expected deficit on Friday, dollar flows were seen continuing positive next week after accumulating a $3.9 billion surplus so far this month.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0917 per dollar, down 0.02 percent.
In the parallel market, the real dropped 0.18 percent to end at 1.140 per dollar, traders said.
